summary: Maintains Project decisions/invariants/advancement, Case facts/impacts/dynamic gaps, Iteration aggregation, and deterministic one-claim transitions with complete invariant assessment.
runtime_notes: Runtime must resolve and call the trusted entrypoints declared by this capability instead of maintaining copied ledger scripts.

Agent-directed Case creation enters through case_control with semantic initial facts, relevant decision/invariant impacts, and at least one gap; ledger allocates ids and atomically registers the v5 Case.

Every Case transition uses a Case-scoped selection token, Case and Project revision binding, complete persisted-candidate accounting, exact selected-gap matching, one acceptance claim, an explicit Project State delta, and complete current invariant assessment.
The ledger validates invariant catalog coverage, duplicate refs, accepted-fact evidence and open-gap bindings; semantic relevance and skill/artifact routing remain Agent-owned.
Different Cases may execute concurrently; Case, Project, iteration, projections, and indexes commit under one cross-process Project lock with rollback.
Iteration v3 contains only Project targets, per-transition accepted Project changes, acceptance state, and Case refs; Loop continuation is forbidden.
Project audits require the complete protocol-defined software decision checklist, core software invariants, durable evidence, and active Case reference alignment.
Concrete project choices settle explicit software decisions; Case-local facts remain in durable artifacts and Case facts, and closed Case history is not accumulated in Project State.

ArcOrbit Runtime passes the Agent Semantic Case Command unchanged to writeback; the trusted entrypoint materializes canonical identity, revision, selected candidate, reverse relations and internal v8 under the Project lock. Direct Agents may still submit v8.
Runtime-owned result, activity, event, and transcript records stay outside the target project; Desktop may pass an arckit-runtime://runs/RUN-... opaque reference for Case round traceability.
Case rendering is content-transparent and dry-run preflights Structured Record round trips plus existing Case index inputs.
Direct Agents and Runtime consume the same manifest-declared loop_snapshot receipt; Runtime does not parse canonical record versions or derive candidates independently.
Successful transition writeback returns an accepted round_closeout with no next candidate, followed by a separately verified post-commit snapshot.

Protocol incompatibility is detected deterministically and handed to the same Agent for semantic reconciliation; trusted writeback binds source digests and commits all canonical replacements atomically.
